executive_summary: The dominant story of the day is the confirmation of an NBA Finals matchup between the New York Knicks and the San Antonio Spurs, a marquee championship pairing that cuts across both the breaking news and newsletter coverage. The Spurs' elimination of the Oklahoma City Thunder to reach the Finals sets the stage for a collision between two of basketball's most storied franchises, generating the kind of cultural moment that commands national attention. The Athletic's newsletter teasing 'Knicks-Spurs, here we go' signals that sports media is already primed to treat this series as a marquee event, amplifying its reach well beyond hardcore basketball audiences. This matters because a Knicks Finals appearance — the franchise's first in decades — transforms the NBA's championship round into a New York story, injecting it into the broader media and cultural conversation at a scale that a smaller-market matchup simply would not.

items.headline: Dijon Chicken With Tomatoes and Scallions
items.blurb: You've heard about my affinity for Dijon mustard, and now I have to confess I love a sweet, juicy burst cherry tomato, too. That makes this recipe from Yasmin a real must-cook for me.

items.headline: Lemony Pasta With Chickpeas and Parsley
items.blurb: Melissa Clark's twist on pasta e ceci is quick, zippy and bright, with a protein boost from the chickpeas that are smushed and simmered into a creamy sauce.

items.headline: Fish and Lentils With Sauce Rof
items.blurb: Trust in Yewande Komolafe: Her sense of flavor and texture will never steer you wrong. She uses sauce rof, the emerald green Senegalese condiment of garlic, herbs, scallions and chile, to add spark to otherwise simple lentils and fish.

items.headline: Quick Shrimp and Asparagus Stir-Fry
items.blurb: This easy spring stir-fry comes from Genevieve Ko, who makes a very good argument for keeping a bag of shrimp on hand in your freezer.

items.headline: Tofu Schnitzel With Buttermilk Slaw
items.blurb: It takes a lot for me to recommend making schnitzel at the end of a busy day, since most versions are messy and cleanup time is a real consideration. But Justine Doiron's recipe is that good, and you can watch her make it here. If you're looking for a little shortcut, you can use packaged coleslaw mix — which is just shredded cabbage and carrot — instead of slicing up cabbage and fennel, though that is truly delicious.

items.headline: Spurs vs. Knicks, starting Wednesday
items.blurb: The Spurs beat the Thunder last night in Oklahoma City, 111-103, setting up a final confrontation with the Eastern Conference champ Knicks that begins on Wednesday in San Antonio. So concludes one of the best Western Conference Finals ever, a true classic.

items.headline: PSG defend European title
items.blurb: The Champions League final mostly went how Arsenal would have hoped, with PSG dominating the ball (75% possession!) but accomplishing little while the Gunners threatened on the counter. But with the score still 1-1 after a listless extra time, the title holders had steadier nerves in the shootout: First Eberechi Eze sent his effort wide after an overcomplicated run-up, then Gabriel fired over to seal a PSG repeat. For neutrals, it's fun that Europe's most entertaining team is also its acknowledged best. For Arsenal, it's another European disappointment.

items.headline: Gauff goes out
items.blurb: The chaos at this French Open is no longer confined to the men's bracket. American defending champ Coco Gauff led in all three sets against Anastasia Potapova but couldn't close out the final two — while playing in front of an oddly sparse crowd because of the Champions League tilt. Afterward, she blamed a lack of killer instinct.

breaking_digest.narrative: The NBA's conference finals are settled: the San Antonio Spurs eliminated the Oklahoma City Thunder to advance to the NBA Finals, where they will face the New York Knicks [1]. The matchup sets up a marquee championship series between two storied franchises, with the Spurs punching through from the Western Conference and the Knicks representing the East. No further details on game scores or series length were immediately available, but the Finals are now locked in [1].
